card.name: Reog Ponorogo
card.tagline: East Javanese masked dance with the giant peacock-tiger mask
card.profile: Reog Ponorogo is a centuries-old theatrical dance from the Ponorogo District of East Java that blends dance, music and mythology (UNESCO; ANTARA). Performers dress as kings, war commanders, knights and horse-mounted warriors to narrate the story of the Bantarangin Kingdom and its king. Its iconic centerpiece is the Dadak Merak (Singo Barong), a huge mask resembling a tiger's head topped with peacock feathers. Traditionally performed at disaster-aversion ceremonies, village cleansings, weddings, circumcisions, thanksgivings, Islamic and national holidays and to welcome guests, it is a source of community pride embodying courage and solidarity.
card.insight: Reog Ponorogo was inscribed on UNESCO's List of Intangible Cultural Heritage in Need of Urgent Safeguarding on 3 December 2024 at the 19th Committee session in Asuncion, Paraguay - Indonesia's 14th element on UNESCO's lists - amid concern that Reog masters are increasingly hard to find (Tempo; UNESCO).
card.image_significance: The peacock-tiger mask of Java. A representative image shows gilded costume, angular hand poses and a temple or court setting — East Java, Indonesia.
